notice: Project-level research framework. Not a NIST standard; no result here is NIST-endorsed. Records marked pending or illustrative carry no verified numbers.

hash.name: Hash-based
hash.problem: Preimage and collision resistance of SHA-2 / SHAKE

code.name: Code-based
code.problem: Syndrome decoding of random or structured codes

schemes.name: ML-KEM
schemes.foundation: Module-LWE over the ring Z_q[X]/(X^256+1), q = 3329
assumptions: Hardness of decisional Module-LWE for the chosen (k, η) parameters
Fujisaki–Okamoto transform modelled in the (quantum) random-oracle model
schemes.limitations: Interpretation pending: literature-reported core-SVP figures are recorded but not reproduced by this project.

schemes.name: ML-DSA
schemes.foundation: Module-LWE and Module-SIS over Z_q[X]/(X^256+1), q = 8380417
assumptions: Module-LWE (key recovery) and Module-SIS / SelfTargetMSIS (forgery)
Fiat–Shamir with aborts in the (quantum) random-oracle model
schemes.limitations: No benchmark case for ML-DSA has a recorded estimate yet.

schemes.name: SLH-DSA
schemes.foundation: Stateless hash-based signatures (SPHINCS+): FORS few-time signatures under a hypertree of WOTS+ / XMSS
assumptions: (Multi-target) preimage, second-preimage and collision resistance of the underlying hash function
Bounded number of signatures per key pair (2^64)
schemes.limitations: Generic hash-attack bounds apply; depth-limited quantum costing (MAXDEPTH) still to be recorded.

schemes.name: FN-DSA (Falcon)
schemes.foundation: NTRU lattices; short-vector sampling via fast Fourier lattice trapdoors
assumptions: NTRU / SIS over NTRU lattices
Correct floating-point Gaussian sampling (implementation-sensitive)
schemes.limitations: Draft standard; parameter details to be confirmed against the final text.

schemes.name: HQC
schemes.standard: Selected March 2025 (NIST IR 8545); draft standard expected
schemes.foundation: Quasi-cyclic syndrome decoding (QCSD) with a concatenated Reed–Muller / Reed–Solomon decoder
assumptions: Hardness of QCSD for the chosen (n, w)
Decryption-failure rate below 2^-128 (reaction attacks otherwise)
schemes.limitations: No ISD cost has been recorded by this project yet.

schemes.name: Classic McEliece
schemes.standard: NIST round 4 (not selected); ISO/IEC standardization track
schemes.foundation: Syndrome decoding of binary Goppa codes
assumptions: Indistinguishability of Goppa codes from random codes
Hardness of syndrome decoding at weight t
schemes.limitations: Only two of the five parameter sets are recorded.

schemes.name: MAYO
schemes.foundation: Oil-and-vinegar multivariate quadratic maps with whipped-up public key
assumptions: Hardness of the (whipped) UOV key-recovery and MQ forgery problems
schemes.limitations: Parameters follow the round-2 submission; MAYO parameters were revised during the competition, so verify the version.

schemes.name: SQIsign
assumptions: Hardness of computing endomorphism rings of supersingular curves
Zero-knowledge of the identification protocol under heuristic assumptions
schemes.limitations: Candidate; sizes follow the round-2 submission.

attacks.name: Primal attack (uSVP embedding) via BKZ
attacks.description: Embed the LWE instance into a lattice whose unique shortest vector reveals the secret, then find it with BKZ at block size β. Cost is dominated by the SVP oracle calls inside BKZ.
assumptions: Core-SVP or gate-count model for one SVP call in dimension β
Geometric-series assumption for the BKZ profile
Success probability targeted by the chosen β

applicability.conditions: Standard LWE embedding; k·n + 1 dimensional lattice
Key recovery from the public key (MLWE); forgery needs the SIS route instead

attacks.name: Dual attack via BKZ
attacks.description: Find short vectors in the dual lattice to distinguish LWE samples from uniform, then recover the secret; modern variants add guessing and FFT post-processing.
assumptions: Dual-lattice BKZ cost model
Statistical assumptions under active scrutiny (2023–24 dual-attack debate)

applicability.conditions: Applies to the MLWE public key
Applies to the MLWE key-recovery problem only

attacks.name: BKZ with quantum sieving
attacks.technique: Lattice reduction with quantum SVP subroutine
attacks.description: Same reduction strategy as the primal or dual attack, but the SVP oracle uses Grover-accelerated sieving (asymptotically 2^0.265β instead of 2^0.292β in the core-SVP model). Quantum memory and depth are charged separately.
assumptions: Quantum random-access memory for the sieve lists
Depth not limited, or MAXDEPTH applied explicitly
Core-SVP exponent 0.265β or a gate-level quantum model

applicability.conditions: Replaces the SVP oracle in the primal attack
Replaces the SVP oracle in the primal attack
Replaces the SVP oracle in the NTRU key-recovery attack

attacks.name: Grover preimage search on the hash function
attacks.description: Search for a preimage of an n-bit hash output with about π/4·2^(n/2) oracle iterations; the only generic quantum speed-up against hash-based signatures. Under a depth limit the attacker must parallelise, losing the square-root gain.
assumptions: Reversible circuit for the hash function
MAXDEPTH budget (2^40, 2^64 or 2^96) when following NIST's metric
Multi-target variant where many hash outputs are available

applicability.conditions: Against WOTS+ chains, FORS leaves or the message digest; parameters n = 16/24/32 bytes set the search space

attacks.name: Parallel collision search (van Oorschot–Wiener)
attacks.description: Memory-efficient parallel collision finding on the hash function at about 2^(n/2) evaluations; relevant where SLH-DSA's security bound involves collision resistance of the tweakable hash.
assumptions: Random-function behaviour of the hash
Distinguished-point memory trade-off

applicability.conditions: Only for components whose bound rests on collision resistance; SLH-DSA is designed to rely mainly on (second-)preimage resistance

attacks.name: Quantum collision finding (BHT)
attacks.description: Brassard–Høyer–Tapp collision finding in about 2^(n/3) queries, but requiring 2^(n/3) quantum-accessible memory; its practical advantage over classical parallel collision search is disputed once memory is costed.
assumptions: Large quantum random-access memory
No depth limit

applicability.conditions: Same components as the classical collision attack

attacks.name: Information-set decoding (Stern / BJMM family)
attacks.description: Guess an information set in which the error vector has low weight and solve by Gaussian elimination, with birthday-style improvements (Stern, MMT, BJMM, May–Ozerov) in the enumeration step.
assumptions: Random-code behaviour of the public code
Memory limits for the list-based variants
For quasi-cyclic codes, a √n DOOM speed-up

applicability.conditions: Against the QCSD problem; DOOM factor applies
Against syndrome decoding at weight t; no quasi-cyclic speed-up

attacks.name: Quantum information-set decoding (Grover-accelerated Prange)
attacks.description: Use Grover search over information sets inside Prange's algorithm, roughly halving the exponent of the simplest ISD; advanced ISD variants gain much less once quantum memory and depth are charged.
assumptions: Reversible Gaussian elimination circuit
Depth and memory accounting per NIST's metrics

attacks.name: Direct algebraic attack (XL / Gröbner basis)
attacks.description: Solve the public quadratic system for a preimage of the target digest with XL or F4/F5 Gröbner-basis algorithms, usually with hybrid guessing of some variables.
assumptions: Semi-regularity of the system (degree of regularity estimate)
Linear-algebra constant for sparse Wiedemann

applicability.conditions: Against the whipped public map; system size depends on k·o

attacks.name: Kipnis–Shamir / reconciliation key recovery
attacks.description: Recover the secret oil subspace from the public map by exploiting the rank structure of the quadratic forms; cost grows with the vinegar-to-oil ratio.
assumptions: Generic behaviour of the public quadratic forms
No additional structure beyond UOV

applicability.conditions: Applies to the underlying UOV map with the small oil space o; MAYO's whipping changes the effective parameters

attacks.name: Classical isogeny-path / endomorphism-ring computation
attacks.description: Find a path in the supersingular ℓ-isogeny graph (or compute the endomorphism ring directly) in roughly p^(1/2) operations; Delfs–Galbraith style algorithms.
assumptions: Generic graph-walk cost
No special structure in the challenge curve

applicability.conditions: Against the secret endomorphism ring; parameter log2 p sets the cost

attacks.name: Quantum isogeny-path computation
attacks.description: Quantum algorithms (Biasse–Jao–Sankar, Tani-style claw finding) lower the exponent to roughly p^(1/4) under generous quantum-memory assumptions.
assumptions: Quantum random-access memory
No depth limit

applicability.conditions: Same problem as the classical path-finding attack
